plan: I will bid my true value, $39. In this 3-bidder third-price auction the winner pays the lowest of the three bids, so if I win my profit is 39 − min(opponents' bids). Bidding above 39 risks winning when the lowest opponent bid exceeds 39 (negative profit); bidding below 39 forgoes profitable wins. With no history and independent draws, truthful bidding balances these risks and maximizes expected long-run profit. Bid must be in $0.1 increments.

[Assume opponents bid their private values uniformly on [0,49]. With two opponents, P(win) = (b/49)^2 when bidding b, and conditional E[min of opponents' bids | both < b] = b/3. Maximize (b/49)^2*(20 - b/3). Taking derivative gives optimum b = 40. Bid 40 to maximize expected profit under these plausible opponent strategies.]

[I assume opponents use symmetric strategies (e.g., bidding their values). If I bid b, win probability = (b/49)^2 and conditional expected payment ≈ b/3, so expected profit = (b/49)^2*(20 - b/3). Maximizing this yields b = 40. Therefore I will bid 40 to balance win probability and expected payment; bidding above value is optimal here because the winner pays the minimum opponent bid.]
